neet_che_u08_t03_1.working: Molecularity is the number of species colliding in an elementary step. It must be a whole number from 1 to 3, so it cannot be zero.

neet_che_u08_t03_3.working: Water is in large excess, so its concentration stays practically constant and is absorbed into k'. The reaction is therefore pseudo first order.

neet_che_u08_t03_4.working: Order is experimental and can be zero or fractional (A-III). Molecularity is theoretical, a whole number 1-3 (B-IV). Pseudo first order means one reactant is in excess (C-II). The rate determining step is the slowest step (D-I).

neet_che_u08_t03_5.working: A is true, since order can be negative (as in Q2). B is false, because molecularity is defined per elementary step, not for a complex reaction. C is true. D is false, because order and molecularity need not be equal. E is true. So A, C and E are correct.
